newsitem.title: USA: Montgomery Ward searching for retail CEO.
newsitem.headline: Montgomery Ward searching for retail CEO.

text.p: Montgomery Ward Holding Corp. said Thursday it has launched a search for an executive to replace Bernard Brennan as chairman and chief executive of the company's lackluster department store unit.
Brennan, who has headed the 400-store chain for the past 11 years, will remain chairman of the parent company, Ward said.
He will retain his ownership of more than one-third of the store chain, Montgomery Ward & Co., and his right to three seats on the board of both the parent and the retail unit.
"He has often said his strengths are in the strategic arena," said company spokeswoman Judy Gustafson. "This gives him that opportunity."
Ward's other large investors include General Electric Capital Corp., with a 50 percent stake, and other company managers.

The New York Times, quoting people close to the company, reported Thursday that Montgomery Ward's equity partners have been disappointed with its poor performance and sought a reorganization to make the retailer more competitive.

The company declined to comment on the report. But it said the change in command stems from its decision last spring to look for new sources of capital, perhaps through an initial public offering of its Signature Group direct marketing division or by attracting new investors.

Montgomery Ward also reportedly considered selling off its retail division, but it has denied those reports. While there has been no change in ownership this year, Brennan had been prepared to step aside if one occurred, Gustafson said.
"It's not out of the blue," she said. "That was something we knew could occur, depending on where we wound up."

Montgomery Ward, traditionally strong in appliances, furniture and electronics, has been weakened by competition from electronics superstores and difficulty absorbing Lechmere, an electronics chain acquired in 1994.

While it has sought to bolster clothing sales by stocking more national brands, Montgomery Ward has lost customers to a revitalised Sears, Roebuck and Co., which was headed by Brennan's older brother Edward until last year.
Montgomery Ward "has no mission," said retail consultant Walter Loeb. "Customers don't know what it stands for anymore."
Brennan said he sees the appointment of a new retail CEO as the next key step in the evolution of the company.
"We began the process with a major turnaround of our business in 1995, the largest management-led LBO in the country in 1988, and the acquisition of Lechmere in 1994," he said in a statement.

"There are other major efforts underway including a substantial refocusing and major redeployment of assets to branded apparel," he said. "While the early apparel transition has been difficult, we are beginning to see some very positive results."

Brennan, 58, joined Montgomery Ward in 1982 as executive vice president of store operations. In 1983, he left to become president of Household Merchandising, Inc. before returning to Montgomery Ward in 1985 as president and CEO.
In 1988, he led the $3.8 billion management buy-out of the company in partnership with GE Capital.
Montgomery Ward's annual sales exceed $7 billion at more than 400 stores in 43 states.
